hook.line: Forty-four stones pack a 9×5 board. From the single empty point in the centre, a wild capturing battle begins.

ch.t: The game that chose a king
p: Fanorona is a traditional game widely played in Madagascar. It is thought to have developed from the Arab world’s alquerque, carried by trade.
A legend even says it decided who would become king — a special game to the island’s people.

tl: Thought to have developed from alquerque
The tale of King Ralambo’s heir
Played across Madagascar, even on boards drawn in the dirt
Computer analysis shows perfect play is a draw

ch.say: Move toward them or away — both capture!
ch.cap: The 9×5 board (fanoron-tsivy); only the centre is empty
p: Approach: move a stone along a line and capture the enemy row in front of it.
Withdrawal: move away and capture the row behind. Chain captures can transform the board.

ch.say: You can practise on smaller boards.
cards: A medium version on a 5×5 board
The 9×5 board — the most popular standard

ch.say: Want to hear the legend of the king?
cards: Feigning illness, the king summoned his sons; the elder, absorbed in a tricky fanorona position, came late — and the younger became king
In 2007 Dutch researchers analysed it by computer and showed it is a draw

ch.say: Tap a card to flip it!
cards: Whole rows go at once — a chain can take ten or more
A traditional handicap: the last winner deliberately gives stones away in the next game
Draw lines on the ground and play with pebbles

p: Join a battle of wits handed down on the island.
